(in-package #:libtmux.internal)

(defclass libtmux:daemon ()
  ((lock :initform (make-lock "owned tmux daemon"))
   (changed :initform (make-condition-variable))
   (state :initform :starting)
   (program :initarg :program)
   (socket :initform nil)
   (directory :initform nil)
   (directory-identity :initform nil)
   (socket-identity :initform nil)
   (notify :initform nil)
   (watch :initform nil)
   (event :initform nil)
   (job :initform nil)
   (probe-client :initform nil)
   (worker :initform nil)
   (pid :initform nil)
   (process-start :initform nil)
   (startup-active :initform t)
   (stop-requested :initform nil)
   (ready-requested :initform nil)
   (job-wake :initform nil)
   (finished :initform nil)
   (cleanup-owner :initform nil)
   (failure :initform nil)
   (cleanup-failures :initform nil)
   (lifetime-token :initform (libtmux:make-cancellation-token)))
  (:documentation "An explicitly owned foreground tmux daemon and its supervisor.
Create it with START-DAEMON and release it with STOP-DAEMON or WITH-DAEMON.
Ordinary connection clients are separate resources; closing one leaves this
daemon alive. The owner retains failed cleanup work until an explicit retry.
See also: LIBTMUX:START-DAEMON, LIBTMUX:STOP-DAEMON, LIBTMUX:WITH-DAEMON."))

(defun call-with-daemon-lock (owner function)
  (call-with-lock (slot-value owner 'lock) function))

(defun call-with-daemon-scope (owner function)
  (let ((normal nil))
    (unwind-protect
         (multiple-value-prog1 (funcall function owner) (setf normal t))
      (handler-case (libtmux:stop-daemon owner)
        (error (condition)
          (if normal (error condition)
              (retain-daemon-cleanup-failure owner condition)))))))

(defmethod print-object ((owner libtmux:daemon) stream)
  (print-unreadable-object (owner stream :type t :identity t)
    (write-string (symbol-name (libtmux:daemon-state owner)) stream)))

(in-package #:libtmux)

(defgeneric error-daemon (condition)
  (:documentation "Return the daemon owner retained by a startup or cleanup failure.
The owner may need STOP-DAEMON even when START-DAEMON did not return. No I/O.
See also: DAEMON-START-FAILED, DAEMON-CLEANUP-FAILED, PENDING-DAEMON-CLEANUPS."))

(define-condition daemon-start-failed (libtmux-error)
  ((daemon :initarg :daemon :reader error-daemon))
  (:documentation "Managed startup failed; ERROR-CAUSE and ERROR-DAEMON retain evidence.
Startup attempts cleanup before propagating this condition. Incomplete cleanup
also remains discoverable through PENDING-DAEMON-CLEANUPS.
See also: ERROR-DAEMON, ERROR-CAUSE, STOP-DAEMON."))

(define-condition daemon-cleanup-failed (cleanup-failed)
  ((resource :initarg :resource :reader error-daemon))
  (:documentation "Owned daemon cleanup is incomplete and remains retryable.
ERROR-DAEMON retains the owner. Inspect DAEMON-CLEANUP-FAILURES and retry
STOP-DAEMON; no replacement daemon is started.
See also: ERROR-DAEMON, DAEMON-CLEANUP-FAILURES, STOP-DAEMON."))

(defun daemon-state (daemon)
  "Return DAEMON's observed lifecycle state without I/O.
States are :STARTING, :READY, :STOPPING, :FAILED and :CLOSED. READY records
completed startup verification, not a promise of future process liveness.
See also: DAEMON-FAILURE, STOP-DAEMON."
  (libtmux.internal::call-with-daemon-lock
   daemon (lambda () (slot-value daemon 'libtmux.internal::state))))

(defun daemon-program (daemon)
  "Return an owned copy of DAEMON's resolved tmux executable path. No I/O.
Pass it as OPEN-CLIENT's :PROGRAM when connecting through DAEMON-SOCKET-PATH.
See also: DAEMON-SOCKET-PATH, OPEN-CLIENT."
  (copy-seq (slot-value daemon 'libtmux.internal::program)))

(defun daemon-socket-path (daemon)
  "Return an owned copy of DAEMON's private socket path, or NIL before allocation.
No I/O. An ordinary client may connect while the owner is READY. Closing that
client leaves the daemon alive; STOP-DAEMON releases the daemon itself.
See also: DAEMON-PROGRAM, OPEN-CLIENT, STOP-DAEMON."
  (let ((path (slot-value daemon 'libtmux.internal::socket)))
    (and path (copy-seq path))))

(defun daemon-failure (daemon)
  "Return DAEMON's retained primary failure condition, or NIL. No I/O.
This shared diagnostic can describe background failure after startup returned.
See also: DAEMON-STATE, DAEMON-CLEANUP-FAILURES."
  (libtmux.internal::call-with-daemon-lock
   daemon (lambda () (slot-value daemon 'libtmux.internal::failure))))

(defun daemon-cleanup-failures (daemon)
  "Return a fresh vector of retained secondary cleanup conditions. No I/O.
Conditions are shared diagnostics, newest first, bounded to sixteen entries.
See also: STOP-DAEMON, DAEMON-FAILURE, PENDING-DAEMON-CLEANUPS."
  (libtmux.internal::call-with-daemon-lock
   daemon (lambda () (coerce (slot-value daemon 'libtmux.internal::cleanup-failures)
                             'simple-vector))))

(defun pending-daemon-cleanups ()
  "Return a fresh vector of owners with incomplete cleanup, without daemon I/O.
The library retains them even when startup leaves through a nonlocal exit.
Successful STOP-DAEMON removes an owner from this collection.
See also: STOP-DAEMON, ERROR-DAEMON."
  (libtmux.internal::require-process-profile)
  (libtmux.internal::pending-daemon-owners))

(defun start-daemon (&key (program "tmux") (environment nil environment-p)
                          working-directory temporary-directory
                          (timeout 30) (output-limit 1048576) cancel-token)
  "Start an owned empty-config daemon on a fresh private socket and await readiness.
Uses the qualified SBCL/Linux backend and explicit /dev/null configuration.
ENVIRONMENT is a finite list/vector of distinct NAME=VALUE strings; omission
copies the caller environment, and NIL selects an empty input environment.
Tmux selectors, socket activation and launcher controls are removed. Caller
locale is preserved; Bash shell metadata is not byte-transparent. Environment
values and the native executable remain trusted application configuration.
WORKING-DIRECTORY defaults to the captured current directory. The owner creates
a fresh directory under TEMPORARY-DIRECTORY (default UIOP's temporary directory).
Its canonical ancestors must be owned by this user or root; writable ancestors
must have the sticky bit. No existing daemon or endpoint is adopted.
TIMEOUT is one startup deadline after input preparation, including version and
readiness IPC. OUTPUT-LIMIT must be at least two bytes: half bounds daemon
lifetime diagnostics; the remainder bounds version/readiness output. Cleanup
adds bounded waits; synchronous setup and scheduling can extend caller wall time.
CANCEL-TOKEN affects startup only; after READY, STOP-DAEMON owns cancellation.
Signals DAEMON-START-FAILED with the original cause and owner on startup failure.
See also: WITH-DAEMON, STOP-DAEMON, ERROR-DAEMON, OPEN-CLIENT."
  (libtmux.internal::require-process-profile)
  (libtmux.internal::start-managed-daemon
   program environment environment-p working-directory temporary-directory
   timeout output-limit cancel-token))

(defun stop-daemon (daemon)
  "Stop and reap DAEMON's owned child, then remove its checked socket and directory.
Idempotent after success; returns no values. Never targets a daemon through a
reusable PID or socket command. A 0.75-second admission wait and a separate
0.75-second worker join precede any retried job cleanup (up to 0.5 seconds).
Synchronous OS calls and scheduling can extend wall time. Failed cleanup signals
DAEMON-CLEANUP-FAILED and retains the owner for retry. Closing an ordinary client
does not call this function. Terminating the daemon does not establish exit of
every pane descendant.
See also: WITH-DAEMON, DAEMON-CLEANUP-FAILURES, PENDING-DAEMON-CLEANUPS."
  (libtmux.internal::require-process-profile)
  (check-type daemon daemon)
  (libtmux.internal::stop-managed-daemon daemon))

(defmacro with-daemon ((name &rest options) &body body)
  "Bind a newly started daemon and stop the original owner on every exit.
Accepts START-DAEMON keyword options and body declarations. Preserves multiple
values and the primary nonlocal exit. A cleanup failure after normal completion
signals; during an existing exit it is retained for explicit inspection/retry.
See also: START-DAEMON, STOP-DAEMON, PENDING-DAEMON-CLEANUPS."
  (let ((owner (gensym "DAEMON")))
    `(let ((,owner (start-daemon ,@options)))
       (libtmux.internal::call-with-daemon-scope ,owner (lambda (,name) ,@body)))))

(in-package #:libtmux.internal)

(defun resize-arguments (width height direction amount amount-p zoom fit)
  (unless (= 1 (count-if #'identity (list (or width height) direction zoom fit)))
    (invalid-argument "Choose one resize mode: dimensions, direction, zoom, or fit"))
  (when (and amount-p (not direction))
    (invalid-argument "Amount requires a resize direction"))
  (cond
    (zoom '("-Z"))
    (fit (list (case fit (:smallest "-a") (:largest "-A")
                 (otherwise (invalid-argument "Fit must be :smallest or :largest")))))
    (direction
     (list (case direction (:left "-L") (:right "-R") (:up "-U") (:down "-D")
             (otherwise (invalid-argument "Direction must be :left, :right, :up or :down")))
           (integer-argument amount 1 2147483647 "Resize amount")))
    (t (append (when width (list "-x" (integer-argument width 1 10000 "Width")))
               (when height (list "-y" (integer-argument height 1 10000 "Height")))))))

(defun operate-on-target (client target model command flags observe options)
  (apply #'perform-command client (list target)
         (append (list command "-t" (physical-target target model)) flags)
         :observe (when observe (observe-target client target)) options))

(defun custom-layout-text (text)
  "Validate the layout header; leave checksum, JSON and geometry validation to tmux."
  (let* ((text (text-argument text "Custom layout" nil))
         (start (position-if-not (lambda (character) (find (char-code character) '(9 10 11 12 13 32))) text))
         (json-p (and start (char= (char text start) #\{))))
    ;; Tmux 3.3a leaves its error pointer unset when legacy header scanning fails.
    (unless (or json-p
                (and (> (length text) 5) (char= (char text 4) #\,)
                     (loop for index below 4 always (find (char text index) "0123456789abcdefABCDEF"))))
      (invalid-argument "Custom layout needs four ASCII hex digits, a comma and a body, or a JSON object"))
    (values text json-p)))

(defun layout-argument (layout)
  (let ((named (cdr (assoc layout '((:even-horizontal . "even-horizontal")
                                    (:even-vertical . "even-vertical")
                                    (:main-horizontal . "main-horizontal")
                                    (:main-vertical . "main-vertical") (:tiled . "tiled"))))))
    (when named (return-from layout-argument (values named nil)))
    (when (consp layout)
      (let ((parts (finite-vector layout "Custom layout")))
        (when (and (= 2 (length parts)) (eq :custom (aref parts 0)))
          (return-from layout-argument (custom-layout-text (aref parts 1))))))
    (invalid-argument "Layout must be a supported keyword or (:custom string)")))

(in-package #:libtmux)

(defun resize-pane (client pane &key width height direction (amount 1 amount-p) zoom
                                    (observe t) cancel-token timeout output-limit)
  "Resize PANE and return a COMMAND-OUTCOME with an optional replacement pane.
Choose cell WIDTH/HEIGHT (1..10000), a DIRECTION and positive AMOUNT, or ZOOM.
DIRECTION is :LEFT, :RIGHT, :UP or :DOWN; AMOUNT defaults to one. ZOOM toggles
the window's zoom state. Modes are exclusive. Tmux may clamp sizes to the
available layout; inspect the observed value. Earlier captures stay unchanged.
Signals INVALID-ARGUMENT, STALE-TARGET or an operational condition."
  (libtmux.internal::operate-on-target
   client pane :pane "resize-pane"
   (libtmux.internal::resize-arguments width height direction amount amount-p zoom nil)
   observe (list :cancel-token cancel-token :timeout timeout :output-limit output-limit)))

(defun resize-window (client window &key width height direction (amount 1 amount-p) fit
                                        (observe t) cancel-token timeout output-limit)
  "Resize physical WINDOW and return an outcome with an optional replacement.
Choose cell WIDTH/HEIGHT (1..10000), a DIRECTION and positive AMOUNT, or FIT
(:SMALLEST or :LARGEST attached client). Modes are exclusive; dimensions are
subject to tmux's layout constraints. A resize sets the window-size option to
manual, as tmux does. Signals INVALID-ARGUMENT, STALE-TARGET or an operational
condition. Observation failure is retained separately from mutation success."
  (libtmux.internal::operate-on-target
   client window :window "resize-window"
   (libtmux.internal::resize-arguments width height direction amount amount-p nil fit)
   observe (list :cancel-token cancel-token :timeout timeout :output-limit output-limit)))

(defun select-layout (client window layout &key (observe t) cancel-token timeout output-limit)
  "Apply LAYOUT to physical WINDOW; return an outcome and optional replacement.
LAYOUT is :EVEN-HORIZONTAL, :EVEN-VERTICAL, :MAIN-HORIZONTAL, :MAIN-VERTICAL,
:TILED, or (:CUSTOM string) containing a tmux layout description. Legacy custom
text requires four ASCII hex digits, a comma and a nonempty body; JSON-object
layouts require a live tmux daemon at least 3.8. Header checks precede I/O;
the existing target preflight checks the daemon version before dispatch.
Text is literal; tmux validates its checksum, JSON and geometry. This unzooms
the window. Signals INVALID-ARGUMENT, UNSUPPORTED-CAPABILITY, STALE-TARGET or
an operational condition. Does not change earlier captured values.

See also: NEXT-LAYOUT, PREVIOUS-LAYOUT, OUTCOME-VALUE."
  (multiple-value-bind (argument json-p) (libtmux.internal::layout-argument layout)
    (libtmux.internal::operate-on-target
     client window :window "select-layout" (list "--" argument) observe
     (append (list :cancel-token cancel-token :timeout timeout :output-limit output-limit)
             (when json-p '(:minimum-version "3.8" :feature :json-layout))))))

(defun next-layout (client window &key (observe t) cancel-token timeout output-limit)
  "Cycle WINDOW to tmux's next layout; return an outcome and optional replacement.
Unzooms the window. Captured values remain unchanged. Signals STALE-TARGET or
an operational condition; follow-up acquisition failure is retained separately."
  (libtmux.internal::operate-on-target
   client window :window "next-layout" nil observe
   (list :cancel-token cancel-token :timeout timeout :output-limit output-limit)))

(defun previous-layout (client window &key (observe t) cancel-token timeout output-limit)
  "Cycle WINDOW to tmux's previous layout; return an outcome and optional replacement.
Unzooms the window. Captured values remain unchanged. Signals STALE-TARGET or
an operational condition; follow-up acquisition failure is retained separately."
  (libtmux.internal::operate-on-target
   client window :window "previous-layout" nil observe
   (list :cancel-token cancel-token :timeout timeout :output-limit output-limit)))

(defpackage #:libtmux.json
  (:use #:cl)
  (:documentation "Bounded JSON interchange for native libtmux query filters.
READ-FILTER accepts a complete JSON string in schema libtmux.lisp.filter/1.
It resolves only registered names, rejects duplicate or unknown members, and
never evaluates input as Lisp code. WRITE-FILTER serializes only compiled
declarative filters; native function predicates are not query documents.")
  (:export
   #:read-filter #:write-filter
   #:invalid-filter-document #:filter-document-limit-exceeded
   #:document-path #:document-limit))

(in-package #:libtmux.json)

(defgeneric document-path (condition)
  (:documentation "Return a fresh vector locating a filter-document error."))

(defgeneric document-limit (condition)
  (:documentation "Return the exhausted document limit name, or NIL."))

(define-condition invalid-filter-document (libtmux:libtmux-error)
  ((path :initarg :path :initform #())
   (limit :initarg :limit :initform nil)
   (received :initarg :received :initform nil))
  (:documentation "A filter document is malformed, unknown, or semantically invalid."))

(define-condition filter-document-limit-exceeded (invalid-filter-document) ()
  (:documentation "A filter document exceeds a configured parsing or query-data limit."))

(defmethod document-path ((condition invalid-filter-document))
  (libtmux.internal::owned-data (slot-value condition 'path)))

(defmethod document-limit ((condition invalid-filter-document))
  (slot-value condition 'limit))

(defparameter *schema* "libtmux.lisp.filter/1")
(defconstant +default-max-input-bytes+ 1048576)
(defconstant +default-max-depth+ 64)
(defconstant +default-max-nodes+ 10000)
(defconstant +default-max-string-length+ 65536)
(defconstant +default-max-membership+ 1000)
(defconstant +default-max-integer-digits+ 128)

(defparameter +root-members+
  '("schema" "model" "registryVersion" "expression"))

(defparameter +model-names+
  '(("session" . :session)
    ("window" . :window)
    ("pane" . :pane)
    ("window-link" . :window-link)
    ("client" . :client)))

(defparameter +operator-names+
  '(("=" . :=) ("<" . :<) ("<=" . :<=) (">" . :>) (">=" . :>=)
    ("in" . :in) ("contains" . :contains) ("starts-with" . :starts-with)
    ("and" . :and) ("or" . :or) ("not" . :not)
    ("present" . :present) ("missing" . :missing)
    ("any" . :any) ("all" . :all) ("none" . :none) ("is" . :is)
    ("regex-search" . :regex-search)
    ("regex-full-match" . :regex-full-match)))

(defparameter +regex-option-names+
  '(("caseInsensitiveMode" . :case-insensitive-mode)
    ("multiLineMode" . :multi-line-mode)
    ("singleLineMode" . :single-line-mode)
    ("extendedMode" . :extended-mode)))

(defstruct (json-object (:constructor make-json-object (entries)))
  entries)

(defun safe-received (value)
  (cond ((and (stringp value) (<= (length value) 80)) (copy-seq value))
        ((and (keywordp value) (<= (length (symbol-name value)) 80)) value)
        (t (type-of value))))

(defun fail-document (message &key path cause limit received)
  (error (if limit 'filter-document-limit-exceeded 'invalid-filter-document)
         :path (coerce (reverse path) 'simple-vector)
         :limit limit
         :cause cause
         :message message
         :outcome nil
         :client nil
         :received (safe-received received)))

(defun checked-limit (value name minimum)
  (unless (and (integerp value) (>= value minimum))
    (fail-document (format nil "~S must be an integer no smaller than ~D"
                           name minimum)
                   :received value))
  value)

(defun bounded-utf-8-size (source limit)
  (let ((size 0))
    (loop for character across source
          for code = (char-code character)
          do (incf size (cond ((<= code #x7f) 1)
                              ((<= code #x7ff) 2)
                              ((<= code #xffff) 3)
                              (t 4)))
             (when (> size limit)
               (fail-document
                (format nil "Filter document exceeds ~D UTF-8 bytes" limit)
                :limit :max-input-bytes :received size)))
    size))

(defun json-delimiter-p (character)
  (member character
          '(#\Space #\Tab #\Return #\Linefeed #\, #\] #\} #\{ #\[)
          :test #'char=))

(defun validate-numeric-token-bounds (source limit)
  (let ((index 0)
        (length (length source))
        (in-string nil)
        (escaped nil))
    (loop while (< index length)
          for character = (char source index)
          do (cond
               (in-string
                (cond (escaped (setf escaped nil))
                      ((char= character #\\) (setf escaped t))
                      ((char= character #\") (setf in-string nil)))
                (incf index))
               ((char= character #\")
                (setf in-string t)
                (incf index))
               ((or (digit-char-p character)
                    (and (char= character #\-)
                         (< (1+ index) length)
                         (digit-char-p (char source (1+ index)))))
                (let ((cursor index))
                  (loop while (and (< cursor length)
                                   (not (json-delimiter-p (char source cursor))))
                        do (incf cursor))
                  (let* ((first-digit
                           (if (char= (char source index) #\-)
                               (1+ index)
                               index))
                         (digits (- cursor first-digit)))
                    (unless (loop for position from first-digit below cursor
                                  always (digit-char-p (char source position)))
                      (fail-document
                       "Filter documents accept integer JSON numbers only"
                       :received (subseq source index cursor)))
                    (when (> digits limit)
                      (fail-document
                       (format nil "A numeric token exceeds ~D decimal digits" limit)
                       :limit :max-integer-digits :received digits))
                    (setf index cursor))))
               (t (incf index))))))

(defun parse-bounded-json (source max-depth max-nodes max-string-length)
  (let ((nodes 0))
    (labels ((checkpoint (path)
               (when (> (incf nodes) max-nodes)
                 (fail-document
                  (format nil "Filter document exceeds ~D JSON nodes" max-nodes)
                  :path path :limit :max-nodes :received nodes)))
             (read-event (parser event value depth path)
               (checkpoint path)
               (case event
                 (:value
                  (if (and (floatp value) (zerop value)) 0 value))
                 (:begin-array
                  (when (> depth max-depth)
                    (fail-document
                     (format nil "Filter document exceeds nesting depth ~D" max-depth)
                     :path path :limit :max-depth :received depth))
                  (let ((items (make-array 4 :adjustable t :fill-pointer 0))
                        (index 0))
                    (loop
                      (multiple-value-bind (next-event next-value)
                          (com.inuoe.jzon:parse-next parser)
                        (cond ((eq next-event :end-array) (return))
                              ((null next-event)
                               (fail-document "Unexpected end of JSON array" :path path))
                              (t
                               (vector-push-extend
                                (read-event parser next-event next-value (1+ depth)
                                            (cons index path))
                                items)
                               (incf index)))))
                    (coerce items 'simple-vector)))
                 (:begin-object
                  (when (> depth max-depth)
                    (fail-document
                     (format nil "Filter document exceeds nesting depth ~D" max-depth)
                     :path path :limit :max-depth :received depth))
                  (let ((entries nil)
                        (seen (make-hash-table :test 'equal)))
                    (loop
                      (multiple-value-bind (next-event key)
                          (com.inuoe.jzon:parse-next parser)
                        (cond ((eq next-event :end-object) (return))
                              ((null next-event)
                               (fail-document "Unexpected end of JSON object" :path path))
                              ((not (eq next-event :object-key))
                               (fail-document "Expected a JSON object member" :path path
                                              :received next-event))
                              ((gethash key seen)
                               (fail-document "A JSON object member occurs more than once"
                                              :path (cons key path) :received key))
                              (t
                               (setf (gethash key seen) t)
                               (multiple-value-bind (value-event member-value)
                                   (com.inuoe.jzon:parse-next parser)
                                 (when (null value-event)
                                   (fail-document "A JSON object member has no value"
                                                  :path (cons key path)))
                                 (push (cons key
                                             (read-event parser value-event member-value
                                                         (1+ depth) (cons key path)))
                                       entries))))))
                    (make-json-object (nreverse entries))))
                 ((:end-array :end-object :object-key)
                  (fail-document "Unexpected JSON structural token" :path path
                                 :received event))
                 (otherwise
                  (fail-document "Unexpected end of JSON input" :path path))))
             (parse-root ()
               (com.inuoe.jzon:with-parser
                   (parser source :max-string-length max-string-length :key-fn nil)
                 (multiple-value-bind (event value)
                     (com.inuoe.jzon:parse-next parser)
                   (when (null event)
                     (fail-document "A filter document must contain one JSON value"))
                   (let ((result (read-event parser event value 1 nil)))
                     (multiple-value-bind (extra-event extra-value)
                         (com.inuoe.jzon:parse-next parser)
                       (declare (ignore extra-value))
                       (when extra-event
                         (fail-document "A filter document must contain one JSON value")))
                     result)))))
      (handler-case (parse-root)
        (com.inuoe.jzon:json-parse-limit-error (cause)
          (fail-document "Jzon exhausted the configured string bound"
                         :limit :max-string-length :cause cause))
        (com.inuoe.jzon:json-error (cause)
          (fail-document "Jzon rejected the filter document" :cause cause))))))

(defun object-member (object name)
  (let ((entry (assoc name (json-object-entries object) :test #'string=)))
    (if entry (values (cdr entry) t) (values nil nil))))

(defun required-object-member (object name path)
  (multiple-value-bind (value present-p) (object-member object name)
    (unless present-p
      (fail-document "A required filter-document member is missing"
                     :path (cons name path) :received name))
    value))

(defun closed-object (object allowed path)
  (unless (json-object-p object)
    (fail-document "Expected a JSON object" :path path :received object))
  (loop for entry in (json-object-entries object)
        for name = (car entry)
        unless (member name allowed :test #'string=)
          do (fail-document "A JSON object member is not allowed"
                            :path (cons name path) :received name))
  object)

(defun external-name (name table description path)
  (unless (stringp name)
    (fail-document (format nil "~A must be a JSON string" description)
                   :path path :received name))
  (let ((entry (assoc name table :test #'string=)))
    (unless entry
      (fail-document (format nil "Unknown ~A" description)
                     :path path :received name))
    (cdr entry)))

(defun model-name (model)
  (car (rassoc model +model-names+ :test #'eq)))

(defun operator-name (operator)
  (car (rassoc operator +operator-names+ :test #'eq)))

(defun field-name (key)
  (string-downcase (symbol-name key)))

(defun registered-wire-field (model name path)
  (unless (stringp name)
    (fail-document "A query field name must be a JSON string"
                   :path path :received name))
  (or (loop for field in (libtmux.internal::model-fields model)
            when (string= name (field-name (libtmux.internal::field-spec-key field)))
              return field)
      (fail-document "The query field is not registered for this model"
                     :path path :received name)))

(defun scalar-json-value (value path)
  (cond ((eq value 'null)
         (fail-document "JSON null is not a scalar query operand"
                        :path path :received :null))
        ((or (stringp value) (integerp value) (eq value t) (null value)) value)
        (t (fail-document "A scalar query operand has an unsupported JSON type"
                          :path path :received value))))

(defun json-array-p (value)
  (and (vectorp value) (not (stringp value))))

(defun regex-wire-spec (value path)
  (closed-object value '("engine" "pattern" "options") path)
  (let ((engine (required-object-member value "engine" path))
        (pattern (required-object-member value "pattern" path))
        (options (required-object-member value "options" path)))
    (unless (and (stringp engine) (string= engine "cl-ppcre"))
      (fail-document "The regex engine must be cl-ppcre"
                     :path (cons "engine" path) :received engine))
    (unless (stringp pattern)
      (fail-document "The regex pattern must be a JSON string"
                     :path (cons "pattern" path) :received pattern))
    (closed-object options (mapcar #'car +regex-option-names+)
                   (cons "options" path))
    (let ((native (list :cl-ppcre (copy-seq pattern))))
      (loop for (name . option) in (json-object-entries options)
            for native-option = (external-name name +regex-option-names+
                                               "regex option"
                                               (cons name (cons "options" path)))
            do (unless (or (eq option t) (null option))
                 (fail-document "A regex option must be a JSON Boolean"
                                :path (cons name (cons "options" path))
                                :received option))
               (setf native (append native (list native-option option))))
      native)))

(defun wire-expression (value model allow-regex max-membership &optional path)
  (unless (and (json-array-p value) (plusp (length value)))
    (fail-document "A query expression must be a nonempty JSON array"
                   :path path :received value))
  (let* ((operator
           (external-name (aref value 0) +operator-names+ "query operator"
                          (cons 0 path)))
         (length (length value)))
    (when (and (member operator '(:regex-search :regex-full-match))
               (not allow-regex))
      (fail-document "Regex query nodes require :ALLOW-REGEX T"
                     :path (cons 0 path) :received operator))
    (labels ((arity (expected)
               (unless (= length expected)
                 (fail-document "A query expression has the wrong arity"
                                :path path :received (1- length))))
             (field (index)
               (registered-wire-field model (aref value index) (cons index path))))
      (case operator
        ((:and :or)
         (cons operator
               (loop for index from 1 below length
                     collect (wire-expression (aref value index) model allow-regex
                                              max-membership (cons index path)))))
        (:not
         (arity 2)
         (list operator
               (wire-expression (aref value 1) model allow-regex max-membership
                                (cons 1 path))))
        ((:present :missing)
         (arity 2)
         (list operator (libtmux.internal::field-spec-key (field 1))))
        ((:any :all :none :is)
         (arity 3)
         (let ((relation (field 1)))
           (unless (eq :relation (libtmux.internal::field-spec-kind relation))
             (fail-document "A relation operator requires a registered relation"
                            :path (cons 1 path) :received (aref value 1)))
           (list operator
                 (libtmux.internal::field-spec-key relation)
                 (wire-expression
                  (aref value 2) (libtmux.internal::field-spec-target relation)
                  allow-regex max-membership (cons 2 path)))))
        (:in
         (arity 3)
         (let ((field (field 1))
               (members (aref value 2)))
           (unless (json-array-p members)
             (fail-document "An IN operand must be a JSON array"
                            :path (cons 2 path) :received members))
           (when (> (length members) max-membership)
             (fail-document
              (format nil "Membership contains more than ~D operands" max-membership)
              :path (cons 2 path) :limit :max-membership
              :received (length members)))
           (list operator (libtmux.internal::field-spec-key field)
                 (map 'simple-vector
                      (lambda (member) (scalar-json-value member (cons 2 path)))
                      members))))
        ((:regex-search :regex-full-match)
         (arity 3)
         (let ((field (field 1)))
           (list operator (libtmux.internal::field-spec-key field)
                 (regex-wire-spec (aref value 2) (cons 2 path)))))
        (otherwise
         (arity 3)
         (let ((field (field 1)))
           (list operator (libtmux.internal::field-spec-key field)
                 (scalar-json-value (aref value 2) (cons 2 path)))))))))

(defun read-filter
    (source
     &key
       (allow-regex nil)
       (max-input-bytes +default-max-input-bytes+)
       (max-depth +default-max-depth+)
       (max-nodes +default-max-nodes+)
       (max-string-length +default-max-string-length+)
       (max-membership +default-max-membership+)
       (max-integer-digits +default-max-integer-digits+))
  "Read one bounded libtmux.lisp.filter/1 JSON string into a compiled filter.
External names resolve through closed registries and are never interned. Regex
nodes are rejected unless ALLOW-REGEX is true and libtmux/regex is loaded.
Parser limits bound UTF-8 input bytes, nesting, JSON nodes, strings, membership
arrays and integer-token digits. Decimal and exponent number syntax is rejected
before conversion. Parser limits do not interrupt CL-PPCRE execution."
  (unless (stringp source)
    (fail-document "READ-FILTER requires a complete JSON string" :received source))
  (unless (or (eq allow-regex t) (null allow-regex))
    (fail-document ":ALLOW-REGEX must be T or NIL" :received allow-regex))
  (checked-limit max-input-bytes :max-input-bytes 1)
  (checked-limit max-depth :max-depth 1)
  (checked-limit max-nodes :max-nodes 1)
  (checked-limit max-string-length :max-string-length 1)
  (checked-limit max-membership :max-membership 0)
  (checked-limit max-integer-digits :max-integer-digits 1)
  (bounded-utf-8-size source max-input-bytes)
  (validate-numeric-token-bounds source max-integer-digits)
  (let ((document (parse-bounded-json source max-depth max-nodes max-string-length)))
    (closed-object document +root-members+ nil)
    (let* ((schema (required-object-member document "schema" nil))
           (model-source (required-object-member document "model" nil))
           (version (required-object-member document "registryVersion" nil))
           (expression-source (required-object-member document "expression" nil)))
      (unless (and (stringp schema) (string= schema *schema*))
        (fail-document "Unsupported filter-document schema"
                       :path '("schema") :received schema))
      (let ((model (external-name model-source +model-names+ "query model"
                                  '("model"))))
        (unless (and (integerp version)
                     (= version libtmux.internal::+registry-version+))
          (fail-document "Unsupported query registry version"
                         :path '("registryVersion") :received version))
        (let ((native (wire-expression expression-source model allow-regex
                                       max-membership '("expression"))))
          (handler-case
              (libtmux.query:compile-filter
               model native
               :max-depth max-depth
               :max-input-visits (* 8 max-nodes)
               :max-membership max-membership
               :max-string-length max-string-length
               :max-retained-characters max-input-bytes)
            (libtmux.query:query-limit-exceeded (cause)
              (fail-document "Native query validation exhausted the document node bound"
                             :path '("expression") :limit :max-nodes
                             :cause cause))
            (libtmux.query:invalid-filter (cause)
              (fail-document "The filter document is not a valid native query"
                             :path '("expression") :cause cause))))))))

(defun write-field (writer key)
  (com.inuoe.jzon:write-value writer (field-name key)))

(defun write-regex-spec (writer spec)
  (com.inuoe.jzon:with-object writer
    (com.inuoe.jzon:write-key writer "engine")
    (com.inuoe.jzon:write-value writer "cl-ppcre")
    (com.inuoe.jzon:write-key writer "pattern")
    (com.inuoe.jzon:write-value writer (second spec))
    (com.inuoe.jzon:write-key writer "options")
    (com.inuoe.jzon:with-object writer
      (loop for (key value) on (cddr spec) by #'cddr
            for name = (car (rassoc key +regex-option-names+ :test #'eq))
            do (com.inuoe.jzon:write-key writer name)
               (com.inuoe.jzon:write-value writer value)))))

(defun write-expression (writer expression)
  (let ((operator (first expression)))
    (com.inuoe.jzon:with-array writer
      (com.inuoe.jzon:write-value writer (operator-name operator))
      (case operator
        ((:and :or)
         (dolist (child (rest expression)) (write-expression writer child)))
        (:not (write-expression writer (second expression)))
        ((:present :missing)
         (write-field writer (second expression)))
        ((:any :all :none :is)
         (write-field writer (second expression))
         (write-expression writer (third expression)))
        (:in
         (write-field writer (second expression))
         (com.inuoe.jzon:with-array writer
           (map nil (lambda (operand)
                      (com.inuoe.jzon:write-value writer operand))
                (third expression))))
        ((:regex-search :regex-full-match)
         (write-field writer (second expression))
         (write-regex-spec writer (third expression)))
        (otherwise
         (write-field writer (second expression))
         (com.inuoe.jzon:write-value writer (third expression)))))))

(defun write-filter-to-stream (filter stream pretty)
  (let* ((description (libtmux.query:explain filter))
         (model (getf description :model))
         (registry-version (getf description :registry-version)))
    (com.inuoe.jzon:with-writer
        (writer :stream stream :pretty pretty :max-depth nil)
      (com.inuoe.jzon:with-object writer
        (com.inuoe.jzon:write-key writer "schema")
        (com.inuoe.jzon:write-value writer *schema*)
        (com.inuoe.jzon:write-key writer "model")
        (com.inuoe.jzon:write-value writer (model-name model))
        (com.inuoe.jzon:write-key writer "registryVersion")
        (com.inuoe.jzon:write-value writer registry-version)
        (com.inuoe.jzon:write-key writer "expression")
        (write-expression writer (libtmux.query:expression filter))))))

(defun open-character-output-stream-p (value)
  (and (streamp value)
       (open-stream-p value)
       (output-stream-p value)
       (nth-value 0 (subtypep (stream-element-type value) 'character))))

(deftype open-character-output-stream ()
  '(and stream (satisfies open-character-output-stream-p)))

(defun write-filter (filter &key stream (pretty nil))
  "Serialize a COMPILED-FILTER as one libtmux.lisp.filter/1 JSON document.
Return a fresh string when STREAM is NIL; otherwise write to the supplied open
output character stream and return NIL without closing it. Pathnames and binary
streams are rejected. The wire contract is native to this port and does not
imply cross-port regex or query equivalence."
  (check-type filter libtmux.query:compiled-filter)
  (when stream (check-type stream open-character-output-stream))
  (if stream
      (progn (write-filter-to-stream filter stream pretty) nil)
      (with-output-to-string (output)
        (write-filter-to-stream filter output pretty))))

(in-package #:libtmux.internal)

(defun binding-command-source (command command-p source source-p)
  (when (eq command-p source-p)
    (invalid-argument "Specify exactly one of command argv or command-source"))
  (if source-p
      (text-argument source "Binding command source" nil)
      (let* ((arguments (argument-vector command))
             (name (when (plusp (length arguments)) (aref arguments 0))))
        (unless (and name (plusp (length name)))
          (invalid-argument "Binding command argv needs a nonempty command name"))
        ;; Tmux recognizes NAME=value after removing quotes from the first token.
        (when (find #\= name)
          (invalid-argument "Binding command names cannot contain =; use command-source for assignments"))
        (tmux-command-text arguments))))

(in-package #:libtmux)

(defun list-commands (client &key command format cancel-token timeout output-limit)
  "Inspect built-in tmux commands; return owned UTF-8 printer text and an outcome.
Omit COMMAND to list all built-ins. COMMAND is an exact name or built-in alias
through tmux 3.5a; unknown selectors produce no rows. From 3.6, unique prefixes
are accepted and unknown/ambiguous selectors fail. Configured command-alias
entries are not listed or expanded by this selector.

FORMAT is explicit tmux format source, without time expansion. #() can start
asynchronous jobs owned by this command client; results may be incomplete and
disconnect cleans up those jobs. Omission uses tmux's human-readable format.
Preserve native escaping, whitespace and after-hook output; this is not a
decoded registry.
Blocks under shared preflight/dispatch limits, never retries and starts no
daemon. Failures retain their outcome; invalid UTF-8 signals DECODING-ERROR.
See also: LIST-KEYS, DISPLAY-MESSAGE, OUTCOME-STDOUT, ERROR-OUTCOME."
  (libtmux.internal::printed-command
   client (append '("list-commands")
                  (when format (list "-F" (libtmux.internal::text-argument format "Command format")))
                  (when command
                    (list "--" (libtmux.internal::text-argument command "Command selector" nil))))
   :cancel-token cancel-token :timeout timeout :output-limit output-limit))

(defun list-keys (client &key table key format cancel-token timeout output-limit)
  "Inspect key bindings; return owned UTF-8 printer text and a command outcome.
Omit TABLE to list every key table. TABLE and KEY are literal strings; native
unknown-table and invalid-key failures remain errors. An unbound valid KEY is
an error except on tmux 3.7 through 3.7c, which return empty text. Those releases
also send a single matching row to the server message log and any selected
frontend's status line instead of stdout. Empty text does not prove absence.
FORMAT is explicit tmux format source
and requires live tmux 3.7 or newer; older daemons signal UNSUPPORTED-CAPABILITY
before payload dispatch. Omission uses the native human-readable listing.

FORMAT has no time expansion. #() can start asynchronous command-client jobs,
whose output may be incomplete and whose cleanup follows client disconnect.
Empty expanded lines may be omitted. Native escaping, whitespace and after-hook
output are preserved; the text is not a parsed or replayable configuration.
Blocks under shared preflight/dispatch limits and never retries. Invalid UTF-8 signals
DECODING-ERROR; operational failures retain their outcome.
See also: BIND-KEY, UNBIND-KEY, LIST-COMMANDS, ERROR-OUTCOME."
  (libtmux.internal::printed-command
   client (append '("list-keys")
                  (when table (list "-T" (libtmux.internal::text-argument table "Key table" nil)))
                  (when format (list "-F" (libtmux.internal::text-argument format "Key format")))
                  (when key (list "--" (libtmux.internal::text-argument key "Key" nil))))
   :minimum-version (when format "3.7") :feature :key-listing-format
   :cancel-token cancel-token :timeout timeout :output-limit output-limit))

(defun bind-key (client key &key (table "prefix") repeat note
                               (command nil command-p) (command-source nil source-p)
                               cancel-token timeout output-limit)
  "Replace TABLE's KEY binding and return a COMMAND-OUTCOME.
TABLE defaults to prefix. KEY, TABLE and optional NOTE are literal strings.
REPEAT enables native key repetition. Supply exactly one of COMMAND argv or
COMMAND-SOURCE, explicit tmux parser source. COMMAND argv owns each argument
and preserves its token boundary; its first token must not contain =.

Tmux parses the binding immediately. Assignments/directives in COMMAND-SOURCE
can change daemon environment before a later parse error. Aliases expand during
binding in both forms and can also introduce parser side effects. Failure is
not rollback. Ordinary stored command nodes run later on a key event with its
native target context; this does not retain captured-handle authority.

Success acknowledges the binding and its hooks, not later key execution.
Blocks under shared preflight/dispatch limits, acquires no observation and
never retries. Native key/source errors and uncertain outcomes remain inspectable.
See also: UNBIND-KEY, LIST-KEYS, SEND-KEYS, ERROR-OUTCOME."
  (libtmux.internal::perform-command
   client nil
   (append (list "bind-key" "-T" (libtmux.internal::text-argument table "Key table" nil))
           (when repeat '("-r"))
           (when note (list "-N" (libtmux.internal::text-argument note "Binding note")))
           (list "--" (libtmux.internal::text-argument key "Key" nil)
                 (libtmux.internal::binding-command-source command command-p command-source source-p)))
   :cancel-token cancel-token :timeout timeout :output-limit output-limit))

(defun unbind-key (client key &key (table "prefix") cancel-token timeout output-limit)
  "Remove exactly one KEY from TABLE and return a COMMAND-OUTCOME.
TABLE defaults to prefix. Both strings are literal. A missing key in an
existing table is a native no-op; an absent table is an error. Removing its last
binding can delete the table, so repeated removal need not succeed. No bulk
deletion, reset or retry is implicit. Blocks under shared preflight/dispatch
limits. Success acknowledges removal and hooks; it cannot undo earlier key
execution. Native errors and uncertain outcomes retain their diagnostics.
See also: BIND-KEY, LIST-KEYS, ERROR-OUTCOME."
  (libtmux.internal::perform-command
   client nil (list "unbind-key" "-T" (libtmux.internal::text-argument table "Key table" nil)
                    "--" (libtmux.internal::text-argument key "Key" nil))
   :cancel-token cancel-token :timeout timeout :output-limit output-limit))

(in-package #:libtmux)

(defgeneric entity-model (entity)
  (:documentation "Return :SESSION, :WINDOW, :PANE, :WINDOW-LINK or :CLIENT. No I/O.
:CLIENT denotes an attached tmux client observation, not a connection scope."))

(defclass snapshot ()
  ((context :initarg :context)
   (generation :initarg :generation)
   (reference :initform (gensym "CAPTURE-"))
   (provenance :initarg :provenance)
   (collections :initform (make-hash-table :test 'eq)))
  (:documentation "A finite captured graph assembled over a recorded acquisition interval.
It contains owned observations, not a transactional view of a changing daemon.
Public accessors are local and return fresh mutable values."))

(defclass entity ()
  ((snapshot :initarg :snapshot)
   (model :initarg :model :reader entity-model)
   (identity :initarg :identity)
   (fields :initarg :fields)
   (relations :initform (make-hash-table :test 'eq)))
  (:documentation "An owned observation from one snapshot; construct through acquisition.
Private slot mutation is unsupported. Refresh returns another observation."))
(defclass session (entity) ()
  (:documentation "A captured physical tmux session.

A session is one observation from a snapshot. Calls that only read it take no
client, never contact tmux and keep working after the client closes. Calls
that change a session take a client first and the captured session next.

#### What is on here

Calls that take a session, or that return one, fall into these groups:

**Finding sessions.** `libtmux:fetch-sessions` captures a fresh snapshot and
returns every session in it, while `libtmux:sessions` reads them from a
snapshot you already hold. `libtmux:session/function` returns the session that
a window link or an attached client belongs to. `libtmux:refresh` returns the
same session from a new capture and signals `libtmux:stale-target` when it has
gone.

`libtmux:fetch-sessions`, `libtmux:sessions`, `libtmux:session/function` and
`libtmux:refresh`

**Reading what a capture recorded.** `libtmux:name` returns the captured name
and whether the capture had one, and `libtmux:id` returns the tmux identity, a
string such as `$0`. `libtmux:field-value` reaches any other registered field,
such as the creation time, the attached count and the window link count, and
`libtmux:entity-data` returns every captured field as a fresh plist.
`libtmux:entity-model` names the kind of entity,
`libtmux:provenance` reports the capture it came from, and
`libtmux:same-entity-p` compares identity, not field values. None of them
contacts tmux.

`libtmux:name`, `libtmux:id`, `libtmux:field-value`, `libtmux:entity-data`,
`libtmux:entity-model`, `libtmux:provenance` and `libtmux:same-entity-p`

**Walking to its windows and terminals.** `libtmux:windows` returns the
session's windows, one per link, so a window linked twice appears twice.
`libtmux:window-links` returns the links, each with an index and an active
flag, and `libtmux:clients` returns the terminals attached to the session.

`libtmux:windows`, `libtmux:window-links` and `libtmux:clients`

**Creating, renaming and removing.** `libtmux:new-session` creates a detached
session on a daemon that is already running; it never starts or replaces one,
and `libtmux:outcome-value` supplies the new session from the result.
`libtmux:new-window` adds a window to a captured session, and
`libtmux:rename-session` renames one, with tmux enforcing its name
restrictions and uniqueness. `libtmux:kill-session` deletes exactly the
captured session after checking its live identity, and never retries.

`libtmux:new-session`, `libtmux:new-window`, `libtmux:rename-session`,
`libtmux:kill-session` and `libtmux:outcome-value`

**Placing windows.** `libtmux:move-window` moves a window link into the
session at a free index, `libtmux:link-window` links a window there as well,
and `libtmux:break-pane` breaks a pane out into a free index of the session.
None of them overwrites an occupied index.

`libtmux:move-window`, `libtmux:link-window` and `libtmux:break-pane`

**Selecting windows and terminals.** `libtmux:next-window`,
`libtmux:previous-window` and `libtmux:last-window` select a window link in the
session, and `libtmux:last-window` signals an error when tmux has no last
window. `libtmux:switch-client` points an attached terminal at the session, and
`libtmux:lock-session` asks the session's attached terminals to run their lock
command. A lock call's success acknowledges the request, not the terminal's
reaction.

`libtmux:next-window`, `libtmux:previous-window`, `libtmux:last-window`,
`libtmux:switch-client` and `libtmux:lock-session`

**Options, hooks and environment.** Give each call `:scope :session` and the
captured session as `:target`. `libtmux:set-option` and `libtmux:unset-option`
write or clear one option, `libtmux:show-option` and `libtmux:show-options`
return decoded values, and `libtmux:show-options-text` returns tmux's printer
text. `libtmux:set-hook`, `libtmux:unset-hook`, `libtmux:show-hooks` and
`libtmux:show-hooks-text` do the same for hooks, and `libtmux:set-environment`,
`libtmux:unset-environment`, `libtmux:remove-environment`,
`libtmux:show-environment` and `libtmux:show-environment-text` do it for the
session's environment table.

`libtmux:set-option`, `libtmux:unset-option`, `libtmux:show-option`,
`libtmux:show-options`, `libtmux:show-options-text`, `libtmux:set-hook`,
`libtmux:unset-hook`, `libtmux:show-hooks`, `libtmux:show-hooks-text`,
`libtmux:set-environment`, `libtmux:unset-environment`,
`libtmux:remove-environment`, `libtmux:show-environment` and
`libtmux:show-environment-text`

**Messages and control connections.** `libtmux:display-message` prints a
message in the context of a captured session, and expands tmux formats only
when you ask. `libtmux.control:open-connection` and
`libtmux.control:with-connection` attach a separate control connection to a
captured session, which needs a daemon at tmux 3.8 or newer.

`libtmux:display-message`, `libtmux.control:open-connection` and
`libtmux.control:with-connection`

**Filtering sessions.** The separately loaded `libtmux/query` system filters
captured sessions locally. `libtmux.query:compile-filter` compiles a filter
form for the `:session` model without evaluating it as Lisp, and
`libtmux.query:matching` returns the sessions that it accepts.
`libtmux.query:one` and `libtmux.query:one-or-none` take the single result.
`libtmux.query:from` copies sessions into a query set, `libtmux.query:where`,
`libtmux.query:where-if` and `libtmux.query:order-by` narrow and order it,
`libtmux.query:items` returns its members, and `libtmux.query:fields` lists the
fields that a session filter can name.

`libtmux.query:compile-filter`, `libtmux.query:matching`, `libtmux.query:one`,
`libtmux.query:one-or-none`, `libtmux.query:from`, `libtmux.query:where`,
`libtmux.query:where-if`, `libtmux.query:order-by`, `libtmux.query:items` and
`libtmux.query:fields`"))
(defclass window (entity) ()
  (:documentation "A physical window shared by zero or more captured links.

A window is one observation from a snapshot. A session holds it at a link, a
session and an index with the window's ID, so one window can sit in several
sessions. Calls that only read a window take no client, never contact tmux and
keep working after the client closes. Calls that change one take a client
first.

#### What is on here

Calls that take a window, or that return one, fall into these groups:

**Finding windows.** `libtmux:fetch-windows` captures a fresh snapshot and
returns each physical window once, and `libtmux:windows` reads them from a
snapshot you already hold. Given a session, `libtmux:windows` returns one
window per link instead. `libtmux:window/function` returns the window of a pane
or a window link, and `libtmux:refresh` returns the same window from a new
capture and signals `libtmux:stale-target` when it has gone.

`libtmux:fetch-windows`, `libtmux:windows`, `libtmux:window/function` and
`libtmux:refresh`

**Reading what a capture recorded.** `libtmux:name`, `libtmux:width` and
`libtmux:height` return the captured name and size, each with whether the
capture had it, and `libtmux:id` returns the tmux identity, a string such as
`@0`. `libtmux:field-value` reaches any other registered field, such as the
layout string and the pane count, and `libtmux:entity-data` returns every
captured field as a fresh plist. `libtmux:entity-model` names the kind of
entity, `libtmux:provenance` reports the capture it came from, and
`libtmux:same-entity-p` compares identity, not field values. None of them
contacts tmux.

`libtmux:name`, `libtmux:width`, `libtmux:height`, `libtmux:id`,
`libtmux:field-value`, `libtmux:entity-data`, `libtmux:entity-model`,
`libtmux:provenance` and `libtmux:same-entity-p`

**Walking to its panes and links.** `libtmux:panes` returns the window's panes
in captured order, and `libtmux:window-links` returns every link to it, one for
each session and index that holds the window.

`libtmux:panes` and `libtmux:window-links`

**Creating, renaming, restarting and removing.** `libtmux:new-window` adds a
window to a captured session, and `libtmux:outcome-value` supplies the new
window from the result. `libtmux:rename-window` renames one, and tmux may
normalize or reject the name. `libtmux:respawn-window` restarts a window as a
single pane, keeping its first pane and destroying the rest, and replaces
running processes only when you pass `:kill`. `libtmux:kill-window` deletes
exactly the captured window and every link to it.

`libtmux:new-window`, `libtmux:rename-window`, `libtmux:respawn-window`,
`libtmux:kill-window` and `libtmux:outcome-value`

**Layout, size and pane order.** `libtmux:select-layout` applies a named or
custom layout, and `libtmux:next-layout` and `libtmux:previous-layout` cycle
through tmux's layouts; all three unzoom the window. `libtmux:resize-window`
sets cell dimensions or fits the window to the smallest or largest attached
client, and it sets the window-size option to manual. `libtmux:rotate-window`
rotates the positions of the panes, and `libtmux:last-pane` selects the
window's last active pane.

`libtmux:select-layout`, `libtmux:next-layout`, `libtmux:previous-layout`,
`libtmux:resize-window`, `libtmux:rotate-window` and `libtmux:last-pane`

**Selecting and placing window links.** A window sits in a session at a link,
so these calls take links from `libtmux:window-links`, or a session.
`libtmux:select-window` selects one link, and `libtmux:next-window`,
`libtmux:previous-window` and `libtmux:last-window` move a session's
selection. `libtmux:swap-windows`, `libtmux:move-window` and
`libtmux:link-window` change where windows sit, and `libtmux:break-pane` breaks
a pane out into a free index. `libtmux:unlink-window` removes one link, and
tmux refuses to remove the last link to a window unless you pass
`:kill-if-last`.

`libtmux:select-window`, `libtmux:next-window`, `libtmux:previous-window`,
`libtmux:last-window`, `libtmux:swap-windows`, `libtmux:move-window`,
`libtmux:link-window`, `libtmux:break-pane` and `libtmux:unlink-window`

**Options and hooks.** Give each call `:scope :window` and the captured window
as `:target`. `libtmux:set-option` and `libtmux:unset-option` write or clear
one option, `libtmux:show-option` and `libtmux:show-options` return decoded
values, and `libtmux:show-options-text` returns tmux's printer text.
`libtmux:set-hook`, `libtmux:unset-hook`, `libtmux:show-hooks` and
`libtmux:show-hooks-text` do the same for hooks. The environment calls accept
only `:global` and `:session` scope.

`libtmux:set-option`, `libtmux:unset-option`, `libtmux:show-option`,
`libtmux:show-options`, `libtmux:show-options-text`, `libtmux:set-hook`,
`libtmux:unset-hook`, `libtmux:show-hooks` and `libtmux:show-hooks-text`

**Printing a message.** `libtmux:display-message` prints a message in the
context of a captured window, and expands tmux formats only when you ask. A
physical window leaves its session context to tmux, so pass a window link when
the session and index matter.

`libtmux:display-message`

**Filtering windows.** The separately loaded `libtmux/query` system filters
captured windows locally. `libtmux.query:compile-filter` compiles a filter form
for the `:window` model without evaluating it as Lisp, and
`libtmux.query:matching` returns the windows that it accepts.
`libtmux.query:one` and `libtmux.query:one-or-none` take the single result.
`libtmux.query:from` copies windows into a query set, `libtmux.query:where`,
`libtmux.query:where-if` and `libtmux.query:order-by` narrow and order it,
`libtmux.query:items` returns its members, and `libtmux.query:fields` lists the
fields that a window filter can name.

`libtmux.query:compile-filter`, `libtmux.query:matching`, `libtmux.query:one`,
`libtmux.query:one-or-none`, `libtmux.query:from`, `libtmux.query:where`,
`libtmux.query:where-if`, `libtmux.query:order-by`, `libtmux.query:items` and
`libtmux.query:fields`"))
(defclass pane (entity) ()
  (:documentation "A physical pane belonging to one captured window.

A pane is one observation from a snapshot. Calls that only read it take no
client, never contact tmux and keep working after the client closes. Calls
that read the screen or change a pane take a client first and the captured pane
next.

#### What is on here

Calls that take a pane, or that return one, fall into these groups:

**Finding panes.** `libtmux:fetch-panes` captures a fresh snapshot and returns
each physical pane once, and `libtmux:panes` reads them from a snapshot you
already hold. Given a window, `libtmux:panes` returns that window's panes in
captured order. `libtmux:window/function` goes the other way, from a pane to
its window, and `libtmux:refresh` returns the same pane from a new capture and
signals `libtmux:stale-target` when it has gone.

`libtmux:fetch-panes`, `libtmux:panes`, `libtmux:window/function` and
`libtmux:refresh`

**Reading what a capture recorded.** `libtmux:index`, `libtmux:width` and
`libtmux:height` return the captured position and size, `libtmux:active-p`
whether the pane was active and `libtmux:dead-p` tmux's dead flag.
`libtmux:current-command` and `libtmux:current-path` return what the pane was
running and where, and `libtmux:title` returns its title. Each returns the
value and whether the capture had it. `libtmux:id` returns the tmux identity, a
string such as `%0`, and `libtmux:field-value` reaches any other registered
field, such as the process ID and the start command. `libtmux:entity-data`
returns every captured field as a fresh plist, `libtmux:entity-model` names the
kind of entity, `libtmux:provenance` reports the capture it came from, and
`libtmux:same-entity-p` compares identity, not field values. None of them
contacts tmux.

`libtmux:index`, `libtmux:width`, `libtmux:height`, `libtmux:active-p`,
`libtmux:dead-p`, `libtmux:current-command`, `libtmux:current-path`,
`libtmux:title`, `libtmux:id`, `libtmux:field-value`, `libtmux:entity-data`,
`libtmux:entity-model`, `libtmux:provenance` and `libtmux:same-entity-p`

**Reading the screen.** `libtmux:capture-pane` reads the pane now, not from the
snapshot, and returns strict UTF-8 text, signalling `libtmux:decoding-error`
for anything else. `libtmux:capture-pane-bytes` returns the octets unchanged.
Both also return the command outcome.

`libtmux:capture-pane` and `libtmux:capture-pane-bytes`

**Driving a pane.** `libtmux:send-text` sends literal text, so C-c stays
literal, and `libtmux:send-keys` interprets tmux key names such as C-c and
Enter. `libtmux:send-prefix` sends the session's prefix key, and
`libtmux:paste-buffer` pastes a tmux buffer. `libtmux:clear-history` clears the
pane's retained history, `libtmux:copy-mode` enters or leaves copy mode, and
`libtmux:pipe-pane` configures a tmux-owned pipe. A completed send means tmux
processed the request, not that the application consumed it.

`libtmux:send-text`, `libtmux:send-keys`, `libtmux:send-prefix`,
`libtmux:paste-buffer`, `libtmux:clear-history`, `libtmux:copy-mode` and
`libtmux:pipe-pane`

**Splitting, restarting and removing.** `libtmux:split-pane` splits a captured
pane, and `libtmux:outcome-value` supplies the new pane from the result.
`libtmux:respawn-pane` restarts the pane's process and replaces a running one
only when you pass `:kill`. `libtmux:kill-pane` deletes exactly the captured
pane and keeps the others.

`libtmux:split-pane`, `libtmux:respawn-pane`, `libtmux:kill-pane` and
`libtmux:outcome-value`

**Selecting and arranging.** `libtmux:select-pane` selects a pane in its
window, and `libtmux:last-pane` selects the window's last active pane.
`libtmux:resize-pane` sets a size, resizes in a direction or toggles zoom, and
`libtmux:swap-panes` swaps two panes. `libtmux:move-pane` and
`libtmux:join-pane` place one pane beside another, destroying a source window
that this empties, and `libtmux:break-pane` breaks a pane out into a free index
of a session.

`libtmux:select-pane`, `libtmux:last-pane`, `libtmux:resize-pane`,
`libtmux:swap-panes`, `libtmux:move-pane`, `libtmux:join-pane` and
`libtmux:break-pane`

**Options and hooks.** Give each call `:scope :pane` and the captured pane as
`:target`. `libtmux:set-option` and `libtmux:unset-option` write or clear one
option, `libtmux:show-option` and `libtmux:show-options` return decoded values,
and `libtmux:show-options-text` returns tmux's printer text.
`libtmux:set-hook`, `libtmux:unset-hook`, `libtmux:show-hooks` and
`libtmux:show-hooks-text` do the same for hooks. The environment calls accept
only `:global` and `:session` scope.

`libtmux:set-option`, `libtmux:unset-option`, `libtmux:show-option`,
`libtmux:show-options`, `libtmux:show-options-text`, `libtmux:set-hook`,
`libtmux:unset-hook`, `libtmux:show-hooks` and `libtmux:show-hooks-text`

**Printing a message.** `libtmux:display-message` prints a message in the
context of a captured pane, and expands tmux formats only when you ask. A
physical pane leaves its session context to tmux.

`libtmux:display-message`

**Filtering panes.** The separately loaded `libtmux/query` system filters
captured panes locally. `libtmux.query:compile-filter` compiles a filter form
for the `:pane` model without evaluating it as Lisp, and
`libtmux.query:matching` returns the panes that it accepts.
`libtmux.query:one` and `libtmux.query:one-or-none` take the single result.
`libtmux.query:from` copies panes into a query set, `libtmux.query:where`,
`libtmux.query:where-if` and `libtmux.query:order-by` narrow and order it,
`libtmux.query:items` returns its members, and `libtmux.query:fields` lists the
fields that a pane filter can name.

`libtmux.query:compile-filter`, `libtmux.query:matching`, `libtmux.query:one`,
`libtmux.query:one-or-none`, `libtmux.query:from`, `libtmux.query:where`,
`libtmux.query:where-if`, `libtmux.query:order-by`, `libtmux.query:items` and
`libtmux.query:fields`"))
(defclass window-link (entity) ()
  (:documentation "A captured session/index locator with its expected physical window ID."))
(defclass attached-client (entity) ()
  (:documentation "One captured attached-tmux-client row; identity is observation-scoped."))

(defgeneric field-value (entity field)
  (:documentation "Return a captured field and presence as two values, without I/O.
Present false is NIL,T; absence is NIL,NIL. Strings and relation containers are
copied. Unknown fields and unloaded relations signal FIELD-UNAVAILABLE."))
(defgeneric entity-data (entity)
  (:documentation "Return a fresh finite plist of captured fields and provenance.
Relationships contain identifiers, not operational handles. Absent optional
fields are omitted; present false values remain in the plist. No tmux I/O."))
(defgeneric id (entity)
  (:documentation "Return the captured identity, copying mutable components. No I/O.
Physical IDs are strings; a link ID is (session-ID index window-ID). Attached
client IDs identify rows within a single observation, not stable daemon clients."))
(defgeneric provenance (observation)
  (:documentation "Return fresh captured provenance and acquisition bounds, without I/O."))
(defgeneric sessions (snapshot)
  (:documentation "Return a fresh vector of physical sessions in captured wire order. No I/O."))
(defgeneric windows (observation)
  (:documentation "Return a fresh vector of captured windows, without I/O.
Snapshot windows are physical entities in first-occurrence order. Session
windows contain one item per link and preserve repeated physical windows."))
(defgeneric panes (observation)
  (:documentation "Return a fresh vector of captured physical panes, without I/O.
Snapshots preserve first occurrence; windows preserve the captured pane order."))
(defgeneric window-links (observation)
  (:documentation "Return every captured window link in wire order as a fresh vector. No I/O."))
(defgeneric clients (observation)
  (:documentation "Return a fresh vector of attached-client observations, without I/O.
Preserve listing order and multiplicity, including repeated target names."))
(defgeneric window (entity)
  (:documentation "Return the locally captured physical window of a pane or link."))
(defgeneric session (entity)
  (:documentation "Return the locally captured session of a link or attached client."))

(defmethod print-object ((snapshot snapshot) stream)
  (print-unreadable-object (snapshot stream :type t :identity t)
    (format stream "generation ~D" (slot-value snapshot 'generation))))
(defmethod print-object ((entity entity) stream)
  (print-unreadable-object (entity stream :type t)
    (prin1 (slot-value entity 'identity) stream)))

(in-package #:libtmux.internal)

(defun owned-data (value)
  (typecase value
    (string (copy-seq value))
    (cons (cons (owned-data (car value)) (owned-data (cdr value))))
    (vector (map 'vector #'owned-data value))
    (t value)))

(defun resolved-field-value (entity registry)
  (let ((field (field-spec-key registry))
        (model (libtmux:entity-model entity)))
    (unless (eq model (field-spec-model registry))
      (error 'libtmux:field-unavailable :field field :model model
             :message (format nil "Field ~S is not registered for model ~S" field model)))
    (if (eq (field-spec-kind registry) :relation)
        (multiple-value-bind (value loaded)
            (gethash field (slot-value entity 'libtmux::relations))
          (unless loaded
            (error 'libtmux:field-unavailable :field field :model model
                   :message (format nil "Relation ~S was not loaded in this capture" field)))
          (values value (if (eq (field-spec-cardinality registry) :many) t (not (null value)))))
        (multiple-value-bind (value present-p)
            (gethash field (slot-value entity 'libtmux::fields))
          (when (and (not present-p) (not (field-spec-optional registry)))
            (error 'libtmux:field-unavailable :field field :model model
                   :message (format nil "Required field ~S is missing from the capture" field)))
          (values value present-p)))))

(defun raw-field-value (entity field)
  (resolved-field-value entity (registered-field field (libtmux:entity-model entity))))

(defun captured-collection (snapshot model)
  (copy-seq (gethash model (slot-value snapshot 'libtmux::collections) #())))

(defun entity-reference (entity)
  (list :model (libtmux:entity-model entity) :id (libtmux:id entity)))

(in-package #:libtmux)

(defmethod field-value ((entity entity) field)
  (multiple-value-bind (value present) (libtmux.internal::raw-field-value entity field)
    (values (if (or (stringp value) (vectorp value)) (copy-seq value) value) present)))
(defmethod id ((entity entity))
  (libtmux.internal::owned-data (slot-value entity 'identity)))
(defmethod provenance ((snapshot snapshot))
  (append (list :context (copy-seq (symbol-name (slot-value snapshot 'context)))
                :generation (slot-value snapshot 'generation)
                :observation (copy-seq (symbol-name (slot-value snapshot 'reference))))
          (libtmux.internal::owned-data (slot-value snapshot 'provenance))))
(defmethod provenance ((entity entity)) (provenance (slot-value entity 'snapshot)))
(defmethod entity-data ((entity entity))
  (append
   (list :libtmux/model (entity-model entity) :libtmux/id (id entity)
         :libtmux/provenance (provenance entity))
   (loop for field in (libtmux.internal::model-fields (entity-model entity))
         append (multiple-value-bind (value present)
                    (field-value entity (libtmux.internal::field-spec-key field))
                  (when present
                    (list (libtmux.internal::field-spec-key field)
                          (if (eq :relation (libtmux.internal::field-spec-kind field))
                              (if (eq :many (libtmux.internal::field-spec-cardinality field))
                                  (map 'vector #'libtmux.internal::entity-reference value)
                                  (libtmux.internal::entity-reference value))
                              value)))))))

(defun same-entity-p (left right)
  "Compare captured identity, not captured field values. No I/O.
Context and generation must agree. Link comparison retains its expected window
and index. Attached clients compare equal only within their original capture."
  (and (typep left 'entity) (typep right 'entity)
       (let ((a (slot-value left 'snapshot)) (b (slot-value right 'snapshot)))
         (and (eq (entity-model left) (entity-model right))
              (eq (slot-value a 'context) (slot-value b 'context))
              (= (slot-value a 'generation) (slot-value b 'generation))
              (or (not (typep left 'attached-client)) (eq a b))
              (equal (slot-value left 'identity) (slot-value right 'identity))))))

(defmethod sessions ((snapshot snapshot)) (libtmux.internal::captured-collection snapshot :session))
(defmethod windows ((snapshot snapshot)) (libtmux.internal::captured-collection snapshot :window))
(defmethod panes ((snapshot snapshot)) (libtmux.internal::captured-collection snapshot :pane))
(defmethod clients ((snapshot snapshot)) (libtmux.internal::captured-collection snapshot :client))
(defmethod window-links ((snapshot snapshot)) (libtmux.internal::captured-collection snapshot :window-link))
(defmethod window-links ((session session)) (field-value session :session/window-links))
(defmethod window-links ((window window)) (field-value window :window/links))
(defmethod clients ((session session)) (field-value session :session/clients))
(defmethod windows ((session session)) (map 'vector #'window (window-links session)))
(defmethod panes ((window window)) (field-value window :window/panes))
(defmethod window ((pane pane)) (field-value pane :pane/window))
(defmethod window ((link window-link)) (field-value link :link/window))
(defmethod session ((link window-link)) (field-value link :link/session))
(defmethod session ((client attached-client)) (field-value client :client/session))

(in-package #:libtmux.internal)

(defmacro define-captured-reader (name documentation &rest bindings)
  `(progn
     (defgeneric ,name (entity) (:documentation ,documentation))
     ,@(loop for (class field) in bindings
             collect `(defmethod ,name ((entity ,class)) (libtmux:field-value entity ,field)))))

(define-captured-reader libtmux:name "Return the captured name and presence, without I/O; text is copied."
  (libtmux:session :session/name) (libtmux:window :window/name) (libtmux:attached-client :client/name))
(define-captured-reader libtmux:active-p "Return captured active state and presence, without I/O. False is NIL,T."
  (libtmux:pane :pane/active) (libtmux:window-link :link/active))
(define-captured-reader libtmux:width "Return the positive captured width and presence, without I/O."
  (libtmux:pane :pane/width) (libtmux:window :window/width))
(define-captured-reader libtmux:height "Return the positive captured height and presence, without I/O."
  (libtmux:pane :pane/height) (libtmux:window :window/height))
(define-captured-reader libtmux:index "Return the nonnegative captured index and presence, without I/O."
  (libtmux:pane :pane/index) (libtmux:window-link :link/index))
(define-captured-reader libtmux:current-command "Return copied captured command text and presence, without I/O."
  (libtmux:pane :pane/current-command))
(define-captured-reader libtmux:current-path "Return copied captured path text and presence, without local pathname conversion."
  (libtmux:pane :pane/current-path))
(define-captured-reader libtmux:title "Return a copied captured pane title and presence; empty is present. No I/O."
  (libtmux:pane :pane/title))
(define-captured-reader libtmux:dead-p "Return tmux's captured dead flag and presence, without inferring it from PID."
  (libtmux:pane :pane/dead))
